decisions.summary: Close the pause-path gap by adding stopWorkspaceDocker calls at both pause call sites (dashboard route and CLI command). Mirrors the pattern established for stop/kill in commit 2d0c4df4a — explicit teardown at the user-initiated lifecycle boundary, not inside stopAgent[Async].

Gate teardown on the same condition that gates the tmux kill: stoppedByPause (dashboard route) / shouldStop (CLI). Pausing an already-stopped agent must NOT touch its Docker stack — it's a pure state-flag flip.

Use the existing stopWorkspaceDocker helper unchanged (docker compose down -v --remove-orphans). Pause semantics match stop/kill — there is no state preservation today (tmux session is killed, runtime is marked stopped), so Docker volume loss on pause is consistent with the existing user-initiated-halt contract. A softer 'docker compose stop' variant is rejected; if state-preserving pause is wanted later it should be a new flag, not the default.

Scope strictly to closing the audit-flagged gap (pause paths). Do NOT pull in original issue items #2 (dashboard surfacing of orphan stacks) or #3 (pan doctor warning) — those are independent enhancements and the issue body itself says 'a teardown-on-stop fix alone resolves the reported symptom.'

Do NOT centralize teardown inside stopAgent / stopAgentAsync. Restart paths (agent-spawner.ts:244, flywheel.ts) call stopAgentAsync and would lose Docker volumes on every restart. The call-site pattern keeps lifecycle teardown explicit and reviewable.

hazards.summary: Pausing an already-stopped agent must not trigger Docker teardown — the stack may already be gone and a needless docker compose down adds spurious warnings.
hazards.mitigation: Gate the stopWorkspaceDocker call on stoppedByPause (dashboard) / shouldStop (CLI), matching the exact same boolean used to gate the tmux kill.

hazards.summary: stopWorkspaceDocker can throw (compose file missing, docker daemon down, timeout). A throw in the lifecycle path must NOT prevent the pause state transition from being persisted.
hazards.mitigation: Wrap the call in try/catch and log a warning (same pattern as routes/agents.ts:1085-1087 and cli/commands/kill.ts:71-73). The pause state must already be persisted before the teardown attempt.

hazards.summary: Restart paths call stopAgentAsync directly (agent-spawner.ts:244-245, flywheel.ts:148). If teardown were centralized into stopAgentAsync, every restart would run 'docker compose down -v' and destroy named volumes (DB data, etc.).
hazards.mitigation: Keep teardown at the user-initiated call site. Document this in the bead description so a future agent doesn't 'helpfully' DRY it up.

hazards.summary: Tests must mock stopWorkspaceDocker — a real docker compose invocation in a unit test would be slow, flaky, and would actually tear down stacks on the CI runner.
hazards.mitigation: Mock '../../../../lib/workspace-manager.js' (route test) and '../../lib/workspace-manager.js' (CLI test) and assert mock call counts and arguments.
